Another thing, I live in the western US and I can tell you that for cows, your description of animals' lives is very far from the truth. Cows live all-but-free lives out here; there are fences to contain them to areas (very often hundreds of square miles big) and sometimes the ranchers will move them from one pasture to the next (move=herd, not pack them into trailers, boxes, ships, etc) but until they are ready to be sold & then butchered, they have pretty much free range.

After they are sold things are very different (they are packed fairly tightly into train cars for transportation usually), but their lives tend to be rather short after that...

Other animals (chickens...) I'm told are NOT treated at all nicely, but I haven't seen those industries first hand so I don't know.
